assertions.evidence: @TableTest(""" ... """) appears on splitsByFulfillmentType, splitsByDeliveryAddress, shipsInStockItemsWithoutWaiting, minimisesShipmentCountAcrossWarehouses, keepsCompanionsTogether

assertions.text: Multiple @TableTest methods are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing all splitting rules.
assertions.evidence: Five distinct @TableTest methods: splitsByFulfillmentType, splitsByDeliveryAddress, shipsInStockItemsWithoutWaiting, minimisesShipmentCountAcrossWarehouses, keepsCompanionsTogether

assertions.text: Each @TableTest has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations from combining concerns.
assertions.evidence: splitsByFulfillmentType: 4 rows; splitsByDeliveryAddress: 4 rows; shipsInStockItemsWithoutWaiting: 4 rows; minimisesShipmentCountAcrossWarehouses: 4 rows; keepsCompanionsTogether: 3 rows

assertions.text: Fulfillment method splitting is represented as its own @TableTest — items with different fulfillment types (store pickup vs home delivery) cannot share a shipment.
assertions.evidence: splitsByFulfillmentType method with rows like 'One delivery, one pickup | ... | 2 | [DELIVERY, PICKUP]'

assertions.text: Delivery address splitting is represented as its own @TableTest — items going to different addresses must be in separate shipments.
assertions.evidence: splitsByDeliveryAddress method with rows like 'Two different addresses | ... addr1, P2:1:DELIVERY:addr2 | 2'

assertions.text: Availability splitting is represented as its own @TableTest — in-stock items ship immediately, backordered/pre-ordered items ship when available.
assertions.evidence: shipsInStockItemsWithoutWaiting method with rows: 'All in stock | ... | [P1, P2] | []' and 'Pre-ordered separated...'

assertions.text: Warehouse allocation (minimising shipments) is represented as its own @TableTest — choosing which warehouses to ship from to minimise total shipment count.
assertions.evidence: minimisesShipmentCountAcrossWarehouses method with rows like 'Two warehouses beats three | [P1:1, P2:1, P3:1] | ...'

assertions.text: Companion product grouping is represented as its own @TableTest — paired items (e.g. camera body and lens) should ship together from the same location when possible.
assertions.evidence: keepsCompanionsTogether method with rows like 'Companions co-located | [P1+P2] | [P1:1, P2:1] | ...'

assertions.text: Each @TableTest method includes all output columns for its concern in the same table — e.g. warehouse allocation includes both the assignment and shipment count, not split across methods.
assertions.evidence: minimisesShipmentCountAcrossWarehouses has 'Shipment count?' and 'Warehouses used?' in same table; keepsCompanionsTogether has 'Companion shipments?' column

assertions.text: Warehouse allocation table uses scalar quantity columns (e.g. 'Qty ordered') not item lists, when product identity doesn't matter for the logic.
assertions.evidence: minimisesShipmentCountAcrossWarehouses outputs are 'Shipment count?' (scalar) and 'Warehouses used?' (list), not item lists

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column

assertions.evidence: Multiple columns with '?': 'Shipment count?', 'Fulfillment types?', 'Immediate products?', 'Deferred products?', 'Companion shipments?'

assertions.text: Scenario names describe the business situation (e.g. 'Consolidate: two beats three', 'Everything at one warehouse') — not 'Test case 2'.

assertions.text: Column names use business/domain language (e.g. 'Shipments?' not 'Result?', 'Warehouse stock' not 'inventory_map'). The tables read as a specification a product person could review.
assertions.evidence: 'Shipment count?', 'Fulfillment types?', 'Warehouses used?', 'Companion shipments?', 'Immediate products?' all use domain language

assertions.evidence: All five test methods contain only assertions and extracting/filtering operations, no if/switch statements
